title: UNIVERSE: Unified Video Action Models for Autonomous Driving with Flexible Mask-Modulated Modality Generation
claim: Existing video-action models use separate or conditionally coupled modules; ours uses one shared network with visibility masking to decouple modalities.
layout: 2x2 grid of dashed panels, three prior and one highlighted ours
description: A 2x2 grid of dashed-border panels comparing how video-frame tokens (green boxes f1..fn) and trajectory/action tokens (orange boxes a1..ak) are denoised. Top-left, 'Separate Video or Trajectory Denoising', shows a green Video DiT and an orange Action DiT side by side with no interaction. Top-right, 'Inverse Dynamics Conditioned on Future Videos', has the Video DiT feeding the Action DiT, with future frames as extra action input. Bottom-left, 'Action-conditioned Video Denoising', reverses that direction. Bottom-right, 'Joint Video & Trajectory Denoising', shows a single blue hatched block, 'UNIVERSE: Shared DiT + Visibility Mask', with both token types above and below it. The blue block stands out from the green and orange modules in the other panels. Token rows sit above and below each block, with C_s marking clean history.
caption: Video-action denoising dependency patterns. Cs denotes clean history and current ego-state conditioning; fi and ai denote video-frame and trajectory tokens. The first three panels illustrate separate or conditionally coupled modules; the last shows UNIVERSE’s shared DiT with future-modality visibility decoupling.
abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) can improve action generalization in autonomous driving by learning scene dynamics through dense future-video supervision. However, deploying such models often requires costly future-video generation, while architectures that bypass video rollout typically separate video and action parameters or alter their learned dependencies at inference. We introduce UNIVERSE, a unified video-action model built on a single mask-modulated Diffusion Transformer (DiT) that combines shared-parameter learning with modality-independent inference. Its Modality-Decoupling Visibility Mask allows future video and trajectory tokens to attend to a common historical context while blocking mutual attention between the two future modalities. As a result, future-video supervision directly updates the parameters used for trajectory denoising, yet video tokens can be omitted at test time without changing the trajectory branch's training-time attention dependencies. The same model supports trajectory-only, video-only, and joint video-action generation. Trajectory-only inference achieves a 4.3x speedup over coupled video-action rollout with comparable planning accuracy. UNIVERSE achieves 91.0 PDMS on NAVSIM, compared with 89.6 for a Two-DiT variant, and demonstrates strong zero-shot transfer to nuScenes and Bench2Drive without target-domain fine-tuning. Controlled ablations further support the complementary benefits of shared parameters, dense video co-training, and modality-decoupled visibility.
